newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call crosses 10 pct on unexpected demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian call crosses 10 pct on unexpected demand.

text.p: Indian call money breached the 10 percent mark in afternoon trade on Thursday on unexpected demand for funds, dealers said.
It opened Thursday in the 4.5-5.0 percent range.
Dealers said call money was quoted between 10.5 and 11.0 percent although deals appeared to have been struck only at the lower end of the range.

They said a few banks which had apparently left some part of their posititons uncovered were scrambling for funds as this was the last day before the reporting day. Banks report their positions to the Reserve Bank of India on Friday.

"Rates have definitely crossed 10 percent but I do not think many deals have been struck," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "Only a few banks seem to have some demand for funds. Most have covered their positions."
Other dealers said the system was feeling the effect of tax payments. They said funds outflow on account of advance tax payments made by companies before December 15 had started.
"Although there has not been any major change in the system, money may have gone out from lending banks," said a dealer. "This could have squeezed supply and led to the firming up of rates."
